entities.summary: Professor Judith Longstaff Mackay is a British physician and tobacco control advocate who has led a campaign against tobacco in Asia since 1984, campaigning for tax increases to discourage youth smoking, for the creation of smoke-free areas, and against tobacco promotion. Her main interests are tobacco in low-income countries, women and tobacco, and challenging the transnational tobacco companies. She is based in Hong Kong, where she is a permanent resident. Judith Mackay was a physicians & medical pioneers from Yorkshire (b. 1943-07-18, Yorkshire). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Judith Mackay's work has led to significant tax increases on tobacco products in Asia, resulting in a decline of youth smoking rates. Her advocacy has also contributed to the creation of smoke-free areas and regulations against tobacco promotion.
